instructions.learn: The Italian Game is one of the oldest recorded chess openings and is still played at the highest level today. We always start with pawn to e4.
After Black responds with e5, the knight develops to f3, attacks the e5-pawn, and helps control the center.
Black develops the knight to c6 and defends the e5-pawn. We now develop the bishop to an active square where it puts pressure on f7.
The move c3 supports a future d4 push, allowing us to challenge Black's control of the center.
instructions.play: Play pawn to c3, preparing d4.

instructions.learn: Instead of playing d4 immediately, we first play d3. This keeps the center solid, supports the e4-pawn, and opens the diagonal for the dark-squared bishop.
instructions.play: Play pawn to d3 and reinforce e4.

instructions.learn: Our kingside pieces are developed, so we can castle. Castling brings the king to safety and connects the rook with the rest of our position.
